# Kneading and gluten

Kneading bread dough develops gluten, the stretchy protein network that traps gas and lets a loaf rise. Strong bread flour with more protein builds more gluten. Well kneaded dough is easier when [[Shaping a boule]].

Stretch a small piece of dough thin between your fingers. If it turns translucent without tearing, the gluten is developed.

Instead of kneading, wet sourdough is strengthened with sets of stretch and folds every half hour during the first rise of [[Proofing dough]].

Whey left over from [[Rennet and curds]] can replace the water in the dough for a softer crumb.
